---
title: "icename-gender"
---

Estimate gender from Icelandic names — from the naming convention and
[Þjóðskrá's name register](https://island.is/leit-i-mannanafnaskra) (Mannanafnaskrá).

```bash
icename-gender name "Helga Ingimundardóttir"      # female  dottir
icename-gender csv people.csv --column name -o people_gender.csv
```

```python
from icename_gender import classify

classify("Helga Ingimundardóttir")   # Estimate(gender='female', rule='dottir', given_name=None)
```

Every estimate comes with the rule that decided it, so results can be reported by how they
were made, and the names no rule decides stay unknown.

::: {.callout-important}
## An estimate from a name, not a fact about a person

This is a simple classifier based on which names the register lists as boys' or girls'
names, and on the *-dóttir*/*-son* convention. It does not infer anyone's sex or gender: it
estimates what a name suggests under naming convention only. Use it for aggregate
statistics, report the unknowns, and never present it as a fact about a person.
:::

## Why Icelandic names are different

Most Icelanders carry no family name. The last name is a patronymic or matronymic — the
father's or mother's given name plus *-dóttir* (daughter) or *-son* (son) — so it says the
bearer's gender outright. And every given name must be approved by the Icelandic Naming
Committee and entered in the register as a boy's name, a girl's name, or a middle name.

Between the two, most Icelandic names can be read without guessing. A general-purpose
name-to-gender tool, trained on first names from other countries, cannot use either.

## What it deliberately does not do

- **No guessing past the evidence.** A name no rule decides is unknown, not a coin toss, and
  a name registered for both boys and girls is not assigned to either.
- **No claims about people.** This estimates gender from a naming convention. Report it in
  aggregate, with the unknowns, never as a fact about an individual.
- **No personal data.** The register is about names, not people. Classifying runs offline
  against a snapshot bundled with the package; nothing is sent anywhere.
